baseline_diagnostic.decision: First-output residence time is overwhelmingly between detokenizer send-start and frontend socket receive in both modes. Earlier Native/Packed delay difference is not stable across diagnostic runs. Candidate intervention pending; no throughput or response-validity acceptance.
limitations: API receive interval includes detokenizer serialization, IPC queueing, event-loop read scheduling and receive-side unpickling; it is not pure tokenization time or proof that tokenization caused all delay.
Boundary stamps are CPU events, not CUDA completion or client-visible first-content delivery. Client TTFT residual contains both pre-API and post-first-output components.
Matched rows have exact per-mode SSE/server ID joins and cross-mode dataset ID, body hash and prompt-token parity; not equal generation trajectories or independent repeats.
900s instrumented n=1 diagnostic does not replace uninstrumented 1200s throughput/SLO acceptance; both response success rates remain below 99%.
Eight per-mode source/GC/memory sidecars were not transferred. Shared source manifest, boot server information and measured timing records were retained.

candidate_serving_validation.analysis_basis: Existing first_output_pipeline_diagnostics recomputed exactly; existing client_stats nearest-rank percentiles. Cross-run matching uses dataset request_id, equal request_body_sha256 and prompt_tokens; within-run server joins use exact captured SSE IDs. Post180 requires server request_received_ts >= each run start+180 in every compared run. No inferred joins or altered success rules.
candidate_serving_validation.decision: Keep default-off candidate for controlled DSV4 text-chat qualification: multi-second receive stall is largely removed and n=1 within-mode request throughput improves. Do not claim a Packed compression speedup: Native and Packed both deliver ~1.729 req/s. Both full-run TTFT-p90 values exceed 10s; Packed misses the unchanged 99% response-validity gate. Missing-output cause remains unresolved.
limitations: n=1, sequential off/on runs at different times and assigned GPU sets on the same host; not a randomized paired throughput estimate.
Replay is closed-loop; faster runs complete more dataset requests. Common-ID latency cohorts control request mix but are conditional on success in every compared run, not the full-run SLO population.
Native and Packed generated completion lengths differ. Client TPOT uses earlier first output, so a larger stream span after this fix does not independently establish slower GPU decode.
Received-to-dispatch includes worker admission, conversion, and dispatch; it is not a separately instrumented tokenizer execution time.
Residual candidate Kernel stalls: 8 successful first packets exceed 1s (max 6.214s); common blocking is largely removed, not every tail cause.
No raw SSE/text or generated token strings retained for the missing-output responses; normal EOS with positive completion usage does not identify parser suppression versus control-only generation.
No mixed tokenizer-endpoint qualification; flag remains off by default. No additional GPU jobs launched by this analysis.
